why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

When one sound is taught in place of a longer item named in the 6th case, it replaces only that item's last sound. Not when the place is itself one sound or a position (उपधा, टि), not for augments, and not for लुक् — the whole suffix goes. (Nyāsa: “आदेशः पुनरत्रैकाल्लभ्यते।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
it describes another word of the rule

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

why.txt: A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

q: from a word in which case?

why.txt: From 4.1.83 to 5.2.140 a taddhita comes, optionally (the phrase stays possible: उपगोरपत्यम्), after the first-named word — the one in the case its defining sentence uses (तस्य in तस्यापत्यम्), not the word for the meaning. From 5.3.1 only the option goes on. (Kāśikā: “वेति किम्? वाक्यमपि हि यथा स्यात्”)

left.txt: a suffix named in a rule stands for the word that ENDS in that suffix (starting from what it was added to) — यञ्-इञोः: a suffix named as the base → यञन्तात् इञन्तात् च — what ends in it (with what it was added to)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). q: from a word in which case?

why.txt: From 4.1.83 to 5.2.140 a taddhita comes, optionally (the phrase stays possible: उपगोरपत्यम्), after the first-named word — the one in the case its defining sentence uses (तस्य in तस्यापत्यम्), not the word for the meaning. From 5.3.1 only the option goes on. (Kāśikā: “वेति किम्? वाक्यमपि हि यथा स्यात्”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

quote.q: `प्रयोजनयोद्धृभ्यः` इति पञ्चम्यन्तत्वात् प्रकृतिनिर्देशः, ततश्च <<समर्थानां प्रथमाद्वा>> [[4.1.82]]  इत्येतद्विरुध्यते; प्रथमस्य प्रत्ययार्थत्वेन द्वितीयस्य प्रकृतित्वेनोपादीयमानत्वादित्यस्य चोद्यस्य निरासायाह - `सोऽस्येति समर्थविभक्तिः प्रत्ययार्थश्चानुवर्तते` इति
'समर्थानां प्रथमाद्वा'  इति वचनात्संग्रामवाचिभ्यः प्रत्ययः प्राप्नोति, न प्रयोजनयोद्धृभ्यश्चरमनिर्दिष्टेभ्य इत्याशङ्क्याह -सोऽस्येति समर्थविभक्तिरित्यादि

why.txt: the suffix named in the 1st case is what is introduced

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

a substitute of more than one sound (or शित्) replaces the WHOLE — it replaces the WHOLE of the place

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
when two lists have the same number of members they pair up IN ORDER (yathāsaṅkhya) — they pair up in order (यथासङ्ख्यम्)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

q: from a word in which case?

why.txt: From 4.1.83 to 5.2.140 a taddhita comes, optionally (the phrase stays possible: उपगोरपत्यम्), after the first-named word — the one in the case its defining sentence uses (तस्य in तस्यापत्यम्), not the word for the meaning. From 5.3.1 only the option goes on. (Kāśikā: “वेति किम्? वाक्यमपि हि यथा स्यात्”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). q: from a word in which case?

why.txt: From 4.1.83 to 5.2.140 a taddhita comes, optionally (the phrase stays possible: उपगोरपत्यम्), after the first-named word — the one in the case its defining sentence uses (तस्य in तस्यापत्यम्), not the word for the meaning. From 5.3.1 only the option goes on. (Kāśikā: “वेति किम्? वाक्यमपि हि यथा स्यात्”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). quote.q: Thus लवणेन संसृष्टः = लवणः 'mixed with salt' as लवणः सूपः 'soup mixed with salt.' So लवणं शाकं, लवणा यवगूः [[1.1.51]]. The लूक् elision takes place when the word लवण is used as a noun, and not as an adjective.

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

From 4.1.83 to 5.2.140 a taddhita comes, optionally (the phrase stays possible: उपगोरपत्यम्), after the first-named word — the one in the case its defining sentence uses (तस्य in तस्यापत्यम्), not the word for the meaning. From 5.3.1 only the option goes on. (Kāśikā: “वेति किम्? वाक्यमपि हि यथा स्यात्”)
